President Erdogan said, We know that the most important problem and complaint of our citizens is the cost of living. It is our duty to prevent the cost of living and not let our citizens get crushed by inflation. (Haberturk)

 

CHP spokesperson Fait Oztrak said, "If the Russia-Ukraine war drags on, serious food security challenges are on our doorstep. We say that a state of emergency should be declared in agriculture this year." (Hurriyet)

 

Treasury and Finance Minister Nureddin Nebati, With this legislation, we have taken a step that paves the way for cryptocurrency in Turkey, but eliminates its damaging aspects, and the business can be carried out with general comprehensive rather than secondary regulations. (All dailies reported)

 

A court ordered the continued detention of philanthropist-businessman Osman Kavala in a case involving the 2013 anti-government Gezi Park protests. (All dailies reported)

 

Dutch PM Rutte will pay an official visit to Turkey today at the invitation of President Erdogan. (All dailies reported)

 

Presidential spokesman Ibrahim Kalin said President Erdogan had offered to mediate to bring Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Vladimir Putin together, adding: "Zelenskyy is open to this offer, but Putin believes that the positions aren t close enough, that the work of the negotiating team should be completed for a meeting at the leaders' level." (NTV)

SUMMARIES

EUD

Submissions for grants are now being accepted under the Supporting Registered Employment Among Women project co-funded by the European Union and Turkey. The project, a ¬29 million initiative drawing on ¬25 million in EU grants, is expected to boost hire rates and jobs among 4,000 women employers and 4,000 women workers across 7 provinces. (Sabah)

 

TURKEY, EU AND EU MEMBER STATES

 

Speaking at the launch of the Horizon Europe Program, Deputy FM and head of European Union Affairs Faruk Kaymakci said, "Our common future and horizon resides in Europe." (TRT Haber)

 

Speaking at TUBITAK's launch of the Horizon Europe Program, Industry and Technology Minister Mustafa Varank said they are working hard to fully honor their commitments to European Union member states the industry's leading investment and trade partner. Varank said Turkey has come of age in terms of achieving integration with the EU, production quality, and meeting its commitments, adding that they understand strengthening ties with the EU during this period is of particular importance. (Dunya)

 

CHP group deputy chair Ozgur Ozel said, Gezi [defendants] had previously been acquitted. They brought Turkey to the point of a country where the defendants can t be acquitted in a case where the judges acquitted them." (T24)

 

Hurriyet columnist Hande Firat interviewed AKP deputy leader Hayati Yazici. Firat wrote, I asked about the detention of Osman Kavala and Selahattin Demirtas, which are frequently raised in EU-Turkey relations... Yazici's statements on this subject will be noted: I have always believed that the judiciary does not do business, does not make decisions that are not necessary, unless necessary. Turkey has accepted the jurisdiction of the European Court of Human Rights. There should be a formulation to meet the requirements of this.

 

Hurriyet wrote, Turkey's peaceful stance and diplomatic initiatives in the war in Ukraine have reflected positively on relations with the EU. EU representatives sent a message to "let's solve the problems, let's get closer again.

 

Sabah reported that the Turkey-EU Joint Parliamentary Commission recently met in Brussels after a four-year hiatus. The meeting praised Turkey's stance on Russia's invasion of Ukraine and its embrace of migrants.

 

The EU, which strives to stand on its own in the field of defense, has approved the Strategic Compass, which will serve as a guide to achieving this goal, reported Hurriyet. The document, which has been revised at least four times in recent months due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, said Turkey has contributed to the Joint Security and Defense Policy (CSDP) missions.

 

Dutch PM Rutte will make an official visit to Turkey today at the invitation of President Erdogan. Erdogan will welcome D Rutte in an official ceremony at Bestepe. (TRTHaber)

 

Italy fully supports Turkey s mediation efforts between Russia and Ukraine, Italian FM Luigi Di Maio said. (TRTHaber)

 

The 2022 Human Rights Award of Dusseldorf Tonhalle was awarded to Osman Kavala at a ceremony. Cem Ozdemir, the German minister of agriculture and food, received the award on Kavala s behalf. (DW Turkce)

 

Turkey delivered a first batch of armored personnel carriers to the Hungarian military. (Ahval)

 

MIGRANTS & REFUGEES

Cumhuriyet wrote, While debate over Hatay s Syrian population continues, many problems from the economy to education are getting attention. Almost everyone in the city agrees that Syrians should return after conditions in their country are restored.

 

Most of the Syrians in Turkey are happy and don t want to go back home, according to a new study.

 

The German government had to take action since tens of thousands of Ukrainian women and children who took refuge there fell into the hands of prostitution gangs and human smugglers. Interior Minister Nancy Feaser announced that they stepped up inspections at stations with uniformed and plainclothes police officers. (Yeni Safak)

 

RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR

Presidential spokesperson Ibrahim Kalin told reporters in Ankara that President Erdogan will consult with NATO leaders on the nearly month-old war. Kalin added that Erdogan is also expected to meet with his US counterpart Joe Biden. (Sabah)

 

AKP spokesperson Omer Celik said, It is possible to address the territorial integrity of Ukraine and Russia s concerns as a whole. There is the possibility and ground to find a balanced way. It should be everyone's duty to empower diplomacy. (Haberturk)

 

Polish President Andrzej Dudasaid on Twitter, As Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has told me, Russians from Syria are coming to UA, and mercenaries from the M.East support Russia. Syrians are the most numerous. He appeals: More NATO assistance to UA is needed! But this also shows RU s weakness and is an interesting signal for Turkey.

 

NATO Secretary-General Jens Stoltenberg praised Turkey s efforts to find a diplomatic solution to Russia s ongoing war on Ukraine. (Daily Sabah)

Lithuanian FM Gabrielius Landsbergis answered a journalist s question, How can you be sure that the sanctions will not be violated by Turkey or Serbia?" by saying: "A very clear message should be given. The same sanctions can be imposed on any country that helps to circumvent the sanctions. We have to be very serious about this." (Sozcu)

 

Some 14,000 Russians have fled to Turkey in just three weeks since the conflict in Ukraine broke out due to what they describe as deteriorating conditions in their country, while more than 49,000 Ukrainians have also arrived in Turkey. (HDN)

 

Izet Ekmekcibasi, head of the Foreign Economic Relations Board s (DEIK) Turkey-Russia Business Council, said Turkish firms are working to replace the US and EU-based brands that withdrew from the Russian market. (Sabah)

 

A superyacht linked to sanctioned Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich was cruising a few kilometers off the coast of southwest Turkey, after skirting European Union waters in recent days, ship tracking data showed. (Duvar English)

 

Unable to return to their countries due to the war and staying in Bodrum, Ukrainian sailors raised the Ukrainian flag near Abramovic's yacht and chanted "No war. (NTV)

 

A new Areda poll asked members of the Turkish public whether they believed NATO could protect Turkey in case of a conflict similar to the one unfolding in Ukraine. 90.8% said that NATO would not be able to support Turkey under similar circumstances. (T24)

 

Turkey s Disaster and Emergency Management Authority (AFAD) set up a mobile kitchen in Lviv, Ukraine to distribute warm food to those in need. (Daily Sabah)

 

DOMESTIC POLITICS

 

Speaking at the Forum Metaverse event, President Erdogan took aim at social media, saying, "Just on their own, the immoral and unlawful actions perpetrated by social media platforms, which have grown into a cartel, are a very clear indication that we absolutely need to plot our own course in this area." (BirGun)

 

The leaders of 6 opposition parties are set to convene for a third time at a dinner hosted by DEVA Party Chair Ali Babacan on Sunday, March 27. At this dinner, where the electoral alliance will be the main topic of conversation, the leaders will have an in-depth discussion on the strategies they might develop in response to the proposed AKP and MHP changes to elections law. (Hurriyet)

 

CHP Deputy Chair Seyit Torun announced that they submitted to parliament an 8-item bill to reinforce the financial structures of municipalities. (Gazete Duvar)

 

A chief judge overseeing the trial of 14 Bogazici University students called the police to the courtroom during a hearing and asked for the lawyers to be removed from the room. (Gercek Gundem)

 

The Turkey Bar Association has said police violence at a protest held by members of the Islamist Furkan Foundation in the southern province of Adana violated a ban on torture and mistreatment," with the Ankara Bar Association filing a complaint against police officers involved in the intervention. (Karar)

 

Turkish prosecutors are seeking jail time for journalist Cihan Yucel and an alleged informant for publishing files exposing corruption within the Youth Foundation of Turkey, an Islamist foundation with close ties to President Erdogan. (Duvar English)

 

THE ECONOMY

 

Labor and Social Security Minister Vedat Bilgin responded to claims that minimum wage earners would be getting a raise mid-year, saying, "The minimum wage gets set in December. Of course, if there were to be extraordinary circumstances, that is an option that can be considered." (T24)

 

Searches for the phrase I want to sell my kidney in Turkey have risen 400% in one year while searches for unemployment benefits soared 5,000% due to the country s economic woes. (BirGun)

 

Following regulatory changes to rules governing food products, the Treasury and Finance Ministry finished drafting legislation to streamline VAT procedures for home buyers. The new model, which is expected to provide much-needed relief to consumers and the industry, will be presented for President Erdogan s approval. (Sabah)

 

All Bus Drivers' Federation head Mustafa Yildirim said that there will be a 20% increase in the price of bus tickets. (Cumhuriyet)

 

In line with the recent price increases in international markets, an increase of up to 30% is expected in the price of natural gas used by the industry. (Dunya)

 

The number of foreigners visiting Turkey was 1.54 million in February, up 186.5% from the same month last year, according to Culture and Tourism Ministry data. (Anadolu Agency)

 

SECURITY NEWS

 

The General Security Directorate has opened bidding on contracts for the purchase of various types of 550,000 tear gas and smoke rounds and 8,000 transparent riot shields. (BirGun)

 

Seven passengers flying to Istanbul Airport were found to be carrying a total of 11 kg of cocaine inside their stomachs. (Hurriyet)

 

CORONAVIRUS

 

Erciyes University Vaccine Research and Development Center head Aykut Ozdarendeli said, Turkovac has proved to be effective against the alpha and delta strains. Our work on the omicron variant of the virus is going at full speed. (HDN)

 

INTERNATIONAL

 

FM Mevlut Cavusoglu said on Twitter, Met with FM Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan of UAE. Discussed bilateral relations and regional developments, especially in Ukraine.

 

A delegation Led by TUSIAD Vice Chair Murat Ozyegin will hold talks in Dubai and Abu Dhabi to develop bilateral economic relations between Turkey and the UAE. (T24)

 

 

WHAT IS EXPECTED?

President Erdogan will attend a mass opening ceremony for World Water Day. Erdogan will receive Dutch PM Mark Rutte. After a one-on-one meeting, the two leaders will hold a joint press conference.

 

FM Mevlüt Çavu_o lu will attend the 48th Foreign Ministers Council Meeting of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) in Pakistan and give a speech.

 

The CHP and MHP will hold parliamentary group meetings.

 

Labor and Social Security Minister Vedat Bilgin will take part in a meeting to promote participation in the production process in Gaziantep.

 

Parliament will debate a bill on consumers rights.

 

Actor Ilyas Salman will face trial in Istanbul on charges of denigrating the Turkish nation, Turkish state, parliament, government,or judicial organs of the state.

 

Journalists Ercan Yeltas and Veysi Altin will face trial in Diyarbakir on charges of spreading terrorist propaganda.

Subject: TURKISH PRESS REVIEW MARCH 22, 2022



 

 

 

HEADLINES

President Erdogan said, We know that the most important problem and complaint of our citizens is the cost of living. It is our duty to prevent the cost of living and not let our citizens get crushed by inflation. (Haberturk)

 

CHP spokesperson Fait Oztrak said, "If the Russia-Ukraine war drags on, serious food security challenges are on our doorstep. We say that a state of emergency should be declared in agriculture this year." (Hurriyet)

 

Treasury and Finance Minister Nureddin Nebati, With this legislation, we have taken a step that paves the way for cryptocurrency in Turkey, but eliminates its damaging aspects, and the business can be carried out with general comprehensive rather than secondary regulations. (All dailies reported)

 

A court ordered the continued detention of philanthropist-businessman Osman Kavala in a case involving the 2013 anti-government Gezi Park protests. (All dailies reported)

 

Dutch PM Rutte will pay an official visit to Turkey today at the invitation of President Erdogan. (All dailies reported)

 

Presidential spokesman Ibrahim Kalin said President Erdogan had offered to mediate to bring Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Vladimir Putin together, adding: "Zelenskyy is open to this offer, but Putin believes that the positions aren t close enough, that the work of the negotiating team should be completed for a meeting at the leaders' level." (NTV)

SUMMARIES

EUD

Submissions for grants are now being accepted under the Supporting Registered Employment Among Women project co-funded by the European Union and Turkey. The project, a ¬29 million initiative drawing on ¬25 million in EU grants, is expected to boost hire rates and jobs among 4,000 women employers and 4,000 women workers across 7 provinces. (Sabah)

 

TURKEY, EU AND EU MEMBER STATES

 

Speaking at the launch of the Horizon Europe Program, Deputy FM and head of European Union Affairs Faruk Kaymakci said, "Our common future and horizon resides in Europe." (TRT Haber)

 

Speaking at TUBITAK's launch of the Horizon Europe Program, Industry and Technology Minister Mustafa Varank said they are working hard to fully honor their commitments to European Union member states the industry's leading investment and trade partner. Varank said Turkey has come of age in terms of achieving integration with the EU, production quality, and meeting its commitments, adding that they understand strengthening ties with the EU during this period is of particular importance. (Dunya)

 

CHP group deputy chair Ozgur Ozel said, Gezi [defendants] had previously been acquitted. They brought Turkey to the point of a country where the defendants can t be acquitted in a case where the judges acquitted them." (T24)

 

Hurriyet columnist Hande Firat interviewed AKP deputy leader Hayati Yazici. Firat wrote, I asked about the detention of Osman Kavala and Selahattin Demirtas, which are frequently raised in EU-Turkey relations... Yazici's statements on this subject will be noted: I have always believed that the judiciary does not do business, does not make decisions that are not necessary, unless necessary. Turkey has accepted the jurisdiction of the European Court of Human Rights. There should be a formulation to meet the requirements of this.

 

Hurriyet wrote, Turkey's peaceful stance and diplomatic initiatives in the war in Ukraine have reflected positively on relations with the EU. EU representatives sent a message to "let's solve the problems, let's get closer again.

 

Sabah reported that the Turkey-EU Joint Parliamentary Commission recently met in Brussels after a four-year hiatus. The meeting praised Turkey's stance on Russia's invasion of Ukraine and its embrace of migrants.

 

The EU, which strives to stand on its own in the field of defense, has approved the Strategic Compass, which will serve as a guide to achieving this goal, reported Hurriyet. The document, which has been revised at least four times in recent months due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, said Turkey has contributed to the Joint Security and Defense Policy (CSDP) missions.

 

Dutch PM Rutte will make an official visit to Turkey today at the invitation of President Erdogan. Erdogan will welcome D Rutte in an official ceremony at Bestepe. (TRTHaber)

 

Italy fully supports Turkey s mediation efforts between Russia and Ukraine, Italian FM Luigi Di Maio said. (TRTHaber)

 

The 2022 Human Rights Award of Dusseldorf Tonhalle was awarded to Osman Kavala at a ceremony. Cem Ozdemir, the German minister of agriculture and food, received the award on Kavala s behalf. (DW Turkce)

 

Turkey delivered a first batch of armored personnel carriers to the Hungarian military. (Ahval)

 

MIGRANTS & REFUGEES

Cumhuriyet wrote, While debate over Hatay s Syrian population continues, many problems from the economy to education are getting attention. Almost everyone in the city agrees that Syrians should return after conditions in their country are restored.

 

Most of the Syrians in Turkey are happy and don t want to go back home, according to a new study.

 

The German government had to take action since tens of thousands of Ukrainian women and children who took refuge there fell into the hands of prostitution gangs and human smugglers. Interior Minister Nancy Feaser announced that they stepped up inspections at stations with uniformed and plainclothes police officers. (Yeni Safak)

 

RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR

Presidential spokesperson Ibrahim Kalin told reporters in Ankara that President Erdogan will consult with NATO leaders on the nearly month-old war. Kalin added that Erdogan is also expected to meet with his US counterpart Joe Biden. (Sabah)

 

AKP spokesperson Omer Celik said, It is possible to address the territorial integrity of Ukraine and Russia s concerns as a whole. There is the possibility and ground to find a balanced way. It should be everyone's duty to empower diplomacy. (Haberturk)

 

Polish President Andrzej Dudasaid on Twitter, As Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has told me, Russians from Syria are coming to UA, and mercenaries from the M.East support Russia. Syrians are the most numerous. He appeals: More NATO assistance to UA is needed! But this also shows RU s weakness and is an interesting signal for Turkey.

 

NATO Secretary-General Jens Stoltenberg praised Turkey s efforts to find a diplomatic solution to Russia s ongoing war on Ukraine. (Daily Sabah)

Lithuanian FM Gabrielius Landsbergis answered a journalist s question, How can you be sure that the sanctions will not be violated by Turkey or Serbia?" by saying: "A very clear message should be given. The same sanctions can be imposed on any country that helps to circumvent the sanctions. We have to be very serious about this." (Sozcu)

 

Some 14,000 Russians have fled to Turkey in just three weeks since the conflict in Ukraine broke out due to what they describe as deteriorating conditions in their country, while more than 49,000 Ukrainians have also arrived in Turkey. (HDN)

 

Izet Ekmekcibasi, head of the Foreign Economic Relations Board s (DEIK) Turkey-Russia Business Council, said Turkish firms are working to replace the US and EU-based brands that withdrew from the Russian market. (Sabah)

 

A superyacht linked to sanctioned Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich was cruising a few kilometers off the coast of southwest Turkey, after skirting European Union waters in recent days, ship tracking data showed. (Duvar English)

 

Unable to return to their countries due to the war and staying in Bodrum, Ukrainian sailors raised the Ukrainian flag near Abramovic's yacht and chanted "No war. (NTV)

 

A new Areda poll asked members of the Turkish public whether they believed NATO could protect Turkey in case of a conflict similar to the one unfolding in Ukraine. 90.8% said that NATO would not be able to support Turkey under similar circumstances. (T24)

 

Turkey s Disaster and Emergency Management Authority (AFAD) set up a mobile kitchen in Lviv, Ukraine to distribute warm food to those in need. (Daily Sabah)

 

DOMESTIC POLITICS

 

Speaking at the Forum Metaverse event, President Erdogan took aim at social media, saying, "Just on their own, the immoral and unlawful actions perpetrated by social media platforms, which have grown into a cartel, are a very clear indication that we absolutely need to plot our own course in this area." (BirGun)

 

The leaders of 6 opposition parties are set to convene for a third time at a dinner hosted by DEVA Party Chair Ali Babacan on Sunday, March 27. At this dinner, where the electoral alliance will be the main topic of conversation, the leaders will have an in-depth discussion on the strategies they might develop in response to the proposed AKP and MHP changes to elections law. (Hurriyet)

 

CHP Deputy Chair Seyit Torun announced that they submitted to parliament an 8-item bill to reinforce the financial structures of municipalities. (Gazete Duvar)

 

A chief judge overseeing the trial of 14 Bogazici University students called the police to the courtroom during a hearing and asked for the lawyers to be removed from the room. (Gercek Gundem)

 

The Turkey Bar Association has said police violence at a protest held by members of the Islamist Furkan Foundation in the southern province of Adana violated a ban on torture and mistreatment," with the Ankara Bar Association filing a complaint against police officers involved in the intervention. (Karar)

 

Turkish prosecutors are seeking jail time for journalist Cihan Yucel and an alleged informant for publishing files exposing corruption within the Youth Foundation of Turkey, an Islamist foundation with close ties to President Erdogan. (Duvar English)

 

THE ECONOMY

 

Labor and Social Security Minister Vedat Bilgin responded to claims that minimum wage earners would be getting a raise mid-year, saying, "The minimum wage gets set in December. Of course, if there were to be extraordinary circumstances, that is an option that can be considered." (T24)

 

Searches for the phrase I want to sell my kidney in Turkey have risen 400% in one year while searches for unemployment benefits soared 5,000% due to the country s economic woes. (BirGun)

 

Following regulatory changes to rules governing food products, the Treasury and Finance Ministry finished drafting legislation to streamline VAT procedures for home buyers. The new model, which is expected to provide much-needed relief to consumers and the industry, will be presented for President Erdogan s approval. (Sabah)

 

All Bus Drivers' Federation head Mustafa Yildirim said that there will be a 20% increase in the price of bus tickets. (Cumhuriyet)

 

In line with the recent price increases in international markets, an increase of up to 30% is expected in the price of natural gas used by the industry. (Dunya)

 

The number of foreigners visiting Turkey was 1.54 million in February, up 186.5% from the same month last year, according to Culture and Tourism Ministry data. (Anadolu Agency)

 

SECURITY NEWS

 

The General Security Directorate has opened bidding on contracts for the purchase of various types of 550,000 tear gas and smoke rounds and 8,000 transparent riot shields. (BirGun)

 

Seven passengers flying to Istanbul Airport were found to be carrying a total of 11 kg of cocaine inside their stomachs. (Hurriyet)

 

CORONAVIRUS

 

Erciyes University Vaccine Research and Development Center head Aykut Ozdarendeli said, Turkovac has proved to be effective against the alpha and delta strains. Our work on the omicron variant of the virus is going at full speed. (HDN)

 

INTERNATIONAL

 

FM Mevlut Cavusoglu said on Twitter, Met with FM Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan of UAE. Discussed bilateral relations and regional developments, especially in Ukraine.

 

A delegation Led by TUSIAD Vice Chair Murat Ozyegin will hold talks in Dubai and Abu Dhabi to develop bilateral economic relations between Turkey and the UAE. (T24)

 

 

WHAT IS EXPECTED?

President Erdogan will attend a mass opening ceremony for World Water Day. Erdogan will receive Dutch PM Mark Rutte. After a one-on-one meeting, the two leaders will hold a joint press conference.

 

FM Mevlüt Çavu_o lu will attend the 48th Foreign Ministers Council Meeting of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) in Pakistan and give a speech.

 

The CHP and MHP will hold parliamentary group meetings.

 

Labor and Social Security Minister Vedat Bilgin will take part in a meeting to promote participation in the production process in Gaziantep.

 

Parliament will debate a bill on consumers rights.

 

Actor Ilyas Salman will face trial in Istanbul on charges of denigrating the Turkish nation, Turkish state, parliament, government,or judicial organs of the state.

 

Journalists Ercan Yeltas and Veysi Altin will face trial in Diyarbakir on charges of spreading terrorist propaganda.
